newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOOD PRICES PUSH S.AFRICAN FEB CPI HIGHER - CSS.
newsitem.headline: FOOD PRICES PUSH S.AFRICAN FEB CPI HIGHER - CSS.

text.p: Higher food prices were one of the main factors behind the rise in consumer inflation in February, the Central Statistical Service said on Thursday.
The service (CSS) released data earlier that showed the consumer price index rose 0.5 percent month-on-month in February compared with a 1.3 percent rise in January.
Year-on-year inflation rose 9.8 percent compared with 9.4 percent previously.
The data was in line with a Reuters consensus poll of economists which forecast a 0.45 percent month-on-month and a 9.75 percent year-on-year increase.
CSS said food prices, which have a 20 percent weighting in the overall index, rose 0.6 percent month-on-month and 10.0 percent year-on-year, contributing 0.1 to the overall monthly increase.
The month-on-month rise was attributed to, among others, a 2.1 percent increase in meat prices, a 2.2 percent rise in milk, cheese and egg prices, and 1.3 percent growth in fruit and nut prices.

Housing, which has a 23 percent weighting, and communication with a 3.2 percent weighting, rose 0.3 percent and 5.2 percent month-on-month respectively and also contributed 0.1 percent to the overall index.
The other items category, which excludes food, housing and communications, contributed the remaining 0.2 percent to the overall index.

CSS noted that in addition to the normal prices surveys for March 1997, it had come to its attention that changed prices of water, electricity, parking fees, car insurance and bus tariffs would also apply.
